subject: Preflight: FinSecure private deployment connectivity and ops checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@finsecure.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Mar 2028 15:02:00 +0000
Subject: Preflight: FinSecure private deployment connectivity and ops checklist

Hi Maria —

Thanks for taking the call today. Quick recap and a short set of asks so your NetOps team can validate the path to a Private VPC deployment (we discussed PrivateLink vs VPC Peering briefly). Please see the checklist attached (redwood-privatenet-ops-checklist.pdf) and the IP allowlist template.

High-level notes from the call:
- FinSecure is prioritizing network isolation and auditability; Private VPC with customer-managed peering looks likely but you asked us to confirm PrivateLink implications for outbound egress.
- Expected QPS: ~120 req/s at 512-token avg per-request during peak.
- Data residency: us-east-1 only for initial rollout.
- Procurement asked for an outline of the network handoff steps so they can estimate lead time.

Immediate asks for NetOps (can you confirm in reply or share a contact we should loop in?):
1) Which connectivity mode does FinSecure prefer — PrivateLink (AWS PrivateLink) or VPC Peering? If leaning Peering, confirm whether cross-account peering is allowed and which CIDR ranges we should avoid.
2) Please confirm the egress policy for outbound calls to public model variant endpoints (if any). Do you require all egress to be NATed through a shared firewall?
3) Fill out the attached ip-allowlist-template.csv with your allowlist IPs for both control-plane callbacks and inference egress (we provided two tabs in the template).
4) If there are existing proxies / TLS inspection devices in the path, note hostnames/port rules so we can schedule a test window.

Next steps I propose: once we get your filled allowlist + preferred connectivity mode we will:
- Provision a temporary test tenant in us-east-1 (Private) for smoke tests.
- Share a minimal network diagram and test plan.
- Schedule a 60-minute connectivity window with your NetOps (app/infra) and our infra engineer (Karthik).

Thanks — attaching the checklist and allowlist template.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Preflight: FinSecure private deployment connectivity and ops checklist

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear notes. A couple quick responses from NetOps:
1) Our preference is VPC Peering for the initial POC because it gives us simpler routing visibility; PrivateLink is interesting but we'd need to see how it fits with our existing service mesh.
2) Egress: All outbound traffic must go through our perimeter NATs and then a firewall for TLS inspection. We cannot allow direct public egress from customer subnets.
3) Filling the CSV — we'll have an initial pass by tomorrow EOD. I’m copying ops@finsecure.com who will own the allowlist.
4) Proxies/TLS inspection: yes, we have a few inline devices; details in the ops mailbox.

A couple of clarifying Qs for Redwood: do you support a model fallback to a smaller instance family if our dedicated pool is saturated? Also what level of KV cache sharing is required across peered VPCs?

Regards,
Maria Gomez
NetOps Lead, FinSecure
maria.gomez@finsecure.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maria Gomez <maria.gomez@finsecure.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 08:14:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Preflight: FinSecure private deployment connectivity and ops checklist

Hi Maria —

Thanks for confirming the leaning to VPC Peering and the egress constraints. A few technical notes / asks from our infra side so we can prepare the test tenant and run a smoke test without hitting your perimeter unexpectedly:

- Peering: we will need the peering account ID and the list of subnets (CIDR) you intend to peer with. Please avoid overlapping /16 ranges; if you can provide /20s or /24s that helps.
- Routing: do you plan to propagate routes via your route tables, or do you prefer we advertise a specific set of routes from our test tenant?
- NAT/Egress: because all inference egress must exit through your perimeter NATs, we need the egress IP prefixes to place in our control plane allowlist (these are the IPs our test workloads will reach out from). If you instead want to whitelist our control-plane callback IPs on your firewall, we can provide just those.
- TLS inspection: if any TLS termination is performed by an inline device that breaks client certificates, we will need a window to run mutual-TLS tests for control-plane callbacks.

On your two questions:
- Model fallback: yes — Redwood supports fallback policies in our routing layer. For the POC we can route to a smaller model-family when Dedicated capacity is saturated, or fall back to a hosted (also restricted) endpoint. We can document the latency/cost tradeoffs.
- KV cache sharing: KV cache is per-runtime and not shared across distinct customer VPCs for security reasons; for peered VPCs you should plan for independent caches unless we set up a shared dedicated cluster (we can discuss).

If you can share the CIDRs and whether route propagation is allowed, we can draft a minimal route map for the smoke test.

Thanks,
Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com
